essence: Always awake: self seen by self; nothing else remains.
Ever-wakefulness: mind wastes; thence true seeing.
Turned back without duality: emperor, sun to ignorance-dark.
Moon eclipsed by own-form joy; inner sense gone: nothing to get.
Understanding and rest firm and clear: aloneness soon.
Rest gained, sorrows ceased, grasper broken: I stand firm in own form.
Risen or absorbed, winner of the nondual taste knows reality.
Self-standing never lost: scripture-squabbles do nothing.
Delusion-freed, living amid people, fear gone: yogin free.

rasa.justification: Seeing without remainder, mind wasted, emperor still, moon eclipsed, understanding at rest, release easy, grasper broken, scriptures impotent, fear gone — every verse stills. Even the first-person seal stands firm rather than exults.

sections.BOUNDARY: No instruction is given; who may teach and what ends rebirth belong to the closing that follows.
sections.EXPLANATION: The fruit in third person then first: always-awake seeing with nothing over; wakefulness equated with mind-wasting, wasting with true seeing; turned back without duality — emperor and sun; moon eclipsed by own-form joy with inner sense gone; understanding and rest firm — aloneness soon; grasp-traces dismissed — release easy; rest gained, sorrows ceased, grasper broken — I stand firm; risen or absorbed — the winner knows; self-standing never lost — scriptures do nothing; delusion shed amid people, fear gone — free while living.
sections.FUNCTION: States the fruit in the third person, then seals it in the first: freedom described, then owned.
sections.KEY TERMS: suprabuddhatva (fully-awake-ness) — equated with mind-wasting; manaskṣaya (mind-wasting) — the equation's hinge; samrāṭ (emperor) — crowned stillness; kevalatā (aloneness) — the near fruit; mokṣalakṣmī (release's fortune) — easy; svarūpastha (abiding in own form) — the first-person seal, refrain-candidate; tattvavit (reality-knower) — risen or absorbed; śāstrabhramaṇa (scripture-wandering) — impotent; vigatabhaya (fear gone) — the standing mark.
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: The wakefulness-method taught before flowers here into standing, seeing, reigning — third person ripening into first.
sections.RELATED: v21 first-person seal flagged for song-setting; v22a silent conjecture followed; Sanderson's nine include vv22-24.
sections.SUMMARY: Always awake sees self by self; waking wastes mind, and wasting yields true seeing. Turned back without duality: emperor, sun. Moon pales before own-form joy; understanding and rest stand firm; release comes easy. Rest gained, sorrows ended, grasper snapped — I stand firm in own form. Risen or gathered, the winner knows; scriptures cannot touch him. Delusion shed, he lives among people, fear gone — free while living.
